hook.text: Engineers have spent decades trying to build walking robots. They keep falling over. Walking is hard.

buildup.text: Bipedal balance requires processing terrain, wind, and inertia every millisecond—a massive control problem.

discovery.text: Boston Dynamics' Atlas can now do backflips, but it still can't match a toddler on rough outdoor ground.

twist.text: Human walking uses passive dynamics—gravity, pendulums, springs—reducing the need for active control.

climax.text: Building a walking machine showed us how elegant evolution's solution really was all along.

punchline.text: Robots proved that walking is engineering genius.

quiz.question: Why is bipedal walking so hard for robots?
options: It requires constant real-time balance adjustments
